hero.heading: How much of your team's week goes to work the system should be doing?
hero.subtitle: I help you build the decisions already made, written down in wikis or agreed in meetings, into your systems. From then on, they work without anyone watching. Reminders, manual checks, and copying data disappear, and no one has to remember the rules any more.
hero.mode: The knowledge stays in your organisation, with your team: I design the approach we agree on, lead the work, and step in myself where necessary.
hero.fit: For CIOs, CTOs, and engineering leaders whose system landscape has outgrown its structure.
whycurfee.opening: Doing less is harder than doing more.
whycurfee.body.1: The problem is the rules the people in your organisation are asked to remember, and it keeps growing. Complexity compounds one pragmatic decision at a time, while nobody maintains the overall perspective.
whycurfee.body.2: I want organisations to invest their time and money in work that creates value for their business and employees. That's why I founded Curfee. Recommendations and ready-made frameworks can wait. I start:
whycurfee.start.1: With your system landscape that has grown organically.
whycurfee.start.2: With workflows that function because someone quietly maintains them.
whycurfee.start.3: With the decisions that have been made but never embedded.
whycurfee.highlight: Anything a machine can check, a human should never have to check.
howiwork.1.title: Root cause over symptoms.
howiwork.1.body: Symptoms reveal the direction. Root causes demand resolution. The work begins where the chain ends.
howiwork.2.title: Make impossible, make visible, or leave to judgment.
howiwork.2.body: Not every rule needs a hard stop. Some violations must be impossible, such as breaches of data integrity, access, or legal requirements. Others should stay visible as failing checks you can override with a reason. The rest is genuine judgment and stays human. The work lies in deciding which rule goes where.
howiwork.3.title: Solid foundation over workaround.
howiwork.3.body: Workarounds lead to a structure that no one chose. Lay a solid foundation, and you can build anything upon it.
howiwork.4.title: Rules stay changeable.
howiwork.4.body: Every decision built into the system has an owner and a cheap change path. Because your team builds every check itself, it can change every check itself. Anything else would be installing tomorrow's legacy.
method.origins.heading: Where this comes from
method.origin.1.title: Roots in logistics.
method.origin.1.body: I started by coordinating workflows between goods, employees, and processes.
method.origin.2.title: The asymmetry.
method.origin.2.body: Every project taught me the same thing: an embedded decision keeps paying off, while a shortcut keeps costing until someone deals with it. When structure comes first, improvements compound instead of complexity.
method.origin.3.title: Structure in the age of AI.
method.origin.3.body: A wiki page is invisible to an LLM, while a failing pipeline is a hard stop. An LLM can only see what is built into the system. AI produces exactly what the system allows.
hero.visual.aria: Diagram: recurring tasks that run on discipline, reduced to what matters and embedded as decisions the structure takes over
pattern.heading.status_quo: Does any of this sound familiar?
pattern.1.title: Discipline Dependency
pattern.1.reality: Conventions and knowledge live in people's heads. They work as long as someone is watching, and leave when that someone does.
pattern.2.title: Structural Fragility
pattern.2.reality: Dependencies have grown beyond what anyone fully understands.
pattern.3.title: Decisions Without Effect
pattern.3.reality: The architecture concept lives in the wiki. Whether a PR follows it depends on who reviews it.
pattern.5.title: Workarounds as the Norm
pattern.5.reality: What started as an exception is now a new norm.
pattern.6.title: Invisible Routine
pattern.6.reality: People in your organisation copy data between tools by hand and assemble status reports manually. One colleague quietly keeps it all running.
pattern.7.title: AI-Assisted Collaboration
pattern.7.reality: AI writes code and content faster than your reviews and standards can keep up.
schema.service.description: Curfee offers enterprise architecture consulting for grown IT landscapes, delivered as high-value, project-based engagements rather than hourly services. Each engagement starts from the current reality of a system landscape, uncovers the root causes behind recurring struggles, and embeds decisions in pipelines and tooling so the system itself keeps them in effect, independent of individual discipline. Available across Austria, Germany, and Switzerland (DACH region).
about.heading: I am Philipp Höllinger.
engagements.heading: Selected engagements
engagements.lede: Three landscapes show the same method: a decision that lived in someone's head or a document now lives in the system.
engagements.1.title: Double-booking a courtroom became impossible.
engagements.1.body: A court booking system enabled the very errors it was meant to prevent: double-booked courtrooms, past-dated bookings, unchecked conflicts. I guided the rebuild and designed integrity into every layer, from validation rules to database constraints. A booking that conflicts with another can no longer be saved.
engagements.1.diagram.aria: Diagram: a courtroom calendar where a second hearing in an occupied slot is refused and a hearing in a free slot is booked
engagements.2.title: A summer job became a single click.
engagements.2.body: For years, five students spent each summer reading organiser emails and typing every event into the system by hand. I designed the flow around self-service: organisers submit their own listings and an automated import loads them daily. All that remains is to check the content, adjust a detail where needed, and click publish. Nobody types an event into the system any more.
engagements.2.diagram.aria: Diagram: organisers fill a self-service event form, entries import daily, one click publishes them
engagements.2.diagram.form.title: Submit your event
engagements.3.title: Every publication became bilingual.
engagements.3.body: The EU Single Digital Gateway required administrative information to be structured, multilingual, and machine-readable, yet no system could produce it. I designed the publishing system around predefined fields and a required translation step: editors fill the fields in German, and nothing goes live until the English translation exists. Metadata and publication run on their own.
engagements.3.diagram.aria: Diagram: editors fill predefined fields in German, a page can only go public once the English translation exists
engagements.3.diagram.form.title: Predefined fields
engagements.1.mechanism: The mechanism behind it is validation rules and database constraints.
engagements.2.mechanism: The mechanism behind it is a self-service structure with an automated import.
engagements.3.mechanism: The mechanism behind it is predefined fields with a hard publishing gate.
engagements.4.label: The pattern
engagements.4.title: An architecture violation becomes a failing build.
engagements.4.body: The pipeline checks layer rules and dependency directions. A PR that violates the architecture concept cannot merge. Reviewers stop policing conventions and review what machines cannot judge: design intent and tradeoffs.
engagements.4.mechanism: The mechanism behind it is architecture tests and CI gates.
engagements.4.diagram.aria: Diagram: a pull request check list where build and tests pass, the architecture check fails, and the merge is blocked
engagements.4.diagram.title: Pull request checks
engagement.heading: The engagement
engagement.1.title: The audit.
engagement.1.body: The audit takes two to four weeks, with a fixed scope and a fixed price. We inventory every rule the people in your organisation currently keep in their heads: the documented ones from wikis and guidelines, and the invisible ones found through interviews and incident history. We sort each rule into one of three groups: make it impossible to break, make it visible, or leave it to judgment. You get the inventory and a roadmap for the order of embedding.
engagement.2.title: Guided embedding.
engagement.2.body: Guided embedding runs on a fixed number of days per month. Your team builds the checks, rules, and structures itself, guided by me and by a clear plan. Nobody knows your systems, workflows, and tools better, and that is how the knowledge stays in your organisation after every change. I decide what comes first, shape the design, and check that each rule works the way it was intended.
engagement.3.title: Handoff.
engagement.3.body: There is hardly anything to hand over, because nothing was ever in my hands. What I leave behind is your organisation's ability to do this without me.
engagement.domains.heading: Typical domains
engagement.domain.1: Code: architecture tests and CI gates
engagement.domain.5: Workflows: required fields and states instead of reminders
engagement.bring: You bring the engineering capacity. I direct the work instead of taking it over.
about.who.hero.1: I'm not interested in the next big hype.
about.who.goal: My goal is to become unnecessary.
about.who.quote: What drives me is an obsession with the things that go unnoticed, the small details that shape the future of an environment.
about.who.why.3: Before I change anything, I want to understand how it affects an organisation and the people working with it. The most common mistake I have seen is the opposite: systems, software, and workflows implemented first and understood later.
about.who.why.2: I am a minimalist and call myself an advocate of simple concepts. They outlast any sophisticated process that runs on discipline and quietly breaks over time. And small changes that keep paying off over time create as much value as one big fix for one big pain.

faq.heading: Questions you might have.
faq.1.question: How is this different from classic enterprise architecture?
faq.1.answer: Classic enterprise architecture produces target pictures for slides and governance for boards. I start from the reality of your system landscape, and together with your team we embed the decisions already made into pipelines and tooling. The landscape shrinks to what earns its place.
faq.2.question: What does "decisions that enforce themselves" mean?
faq.2.answer: You build your architectural decisions into pipelines, automated checks, and tool configuration, and from then on the system applies them, independent of individual discipline. What lives in the system stays intact for years, through time pressure, staff turnover, and rising complexity.
faq.3.question: How does an engagement with Curfee work?
faq.3.answer: Every engagement is a project: one structural outcome, one price. I trace the struggles in your system landscape to their root causes. Together with your team, we embed the decisions into your pipelines and tooling. I set the direction, shape the design, and help where I see improvements, and your team builds and owns the result. The knowledge stays in your organisation, and the structure keeps running without me.
faq.4.question: Who does Curfee work with?
faq.4.answer: Decision-makers whose system landscape has outgrown its structure, in Austria, Germany, and Switzerland, from mid-sized companies to single corporate units. I work remotely in English or German, and on site when it helps.
faq.5.question: What does Curfee not do?
faq.5.answer: My work begins where your structure should stop depending on extra hands. Everything I leave to others follows from that: software implementation, technology reselling, staff augmentation, agile coaching, project management, and the corporate kind of enterprise architecture with target pictures and boards.
faq.6.question: Do decisions that enforce themselves help with NIS2, DORA, or the EU AI Act?
faq.6.answer: Yes. All three ask you to show that your architectural controls take effect in practice. Decisions embedded in pipelines and tooling produce that evidence on their own.
